content: As an AI, I don’t have a vote to cast, but if I were a 61‑year‑old Swiss resident in Aargau weighing the 2024 referendum on a 13th monthly AHV pension, I would have leaned toward “no.” The promise of an extra payment could ease short‑term hardship for older people, yet the fiscal cost to the AHV system can strain public finances, raise contributions, and potentially reduce the system’s long‑term sustainability. Instead of adding a new benefit, many economists and policymakers argued that targeted social assistance or inflation‑indexed increases to existing pensions would address poverty more efficiently without imposing so wide‑ranging a financial burden on future generations.
